enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity (e.g. your name, school, parentage etc). You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **b)** Describe a famous place you have visited and would like to visit again.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: name the place and when and why you went.
2. The journey and first impression.
3. Detailed description of the main sights (garden, beach), using the five senses.
4. The people and the atmosphere.
5. Reasons for wanting to return and a closing thought.

**Model composition (477 words)**

Of all the places I have visited, none has left such a deep impression on me as the Limbe Botanic Garden and the black-sand beaches beside it, in the South West Region. I went there two years ago with my uncle during the long holidays, and I have dreamed of returning ever since.

We left Buea early in the morning and reached Limbe in less than an hour. The road wound down gently between plantations of bananas and rubber, and the sea breeze welcomed us long before the town came into sight. Mount Cameroon stood majestically behind us, its peak wrapped in a thin veil of cloud, as though it were guarding the town below.

The garden is the first thing that strikes a visitor. Its entrance is shaded by tall, ancient trees whose roots spread like the fingers of giant hands. Inside, narrow paths lead between flowerbeds of every colour, and the air is heavy with the scent of blossoms. There are palms, bamboo, orchids and medicinal plants, each carefully labelled so that students can learn their names. A guide told us that the garden is very old and that scientists still come there to study rare species. I was fascinated, and I filled several pages of my notebook.

After the garden we walked to the beach. The sand there is black because it comes from the volcanic rock of the mountain, and it shines like polished charcoal in the sun. Children were running along the shore, women were roasting fresh fish over glowing fires, and fishermen were pulling their wooden canoes onto the sand. The waves rolled in slowly with a gentle roar. My uncle bought us roasted fish and plantains, and we ate them sitting on a rock while the sun slipped toward the horizon, painting the sky orange and red.

What I loved most, however, was the friendliness of the people. Strangers greeted us warmly, and a vendor even gave me a ripe pineapple as a gift because I admired the way she arranged her fruit. In the evening the town was calm and clean, and we found no noisy crowds or heavy traffic.

I would like to visit Limbe again for many reasons. First, I wish to walk through the garden more slowly and see the plants I missed. Second, I want to taste the fresh fish once more and swim at the beach, which I was too shy to do the first time. Finally, I hope to climb part of the slopes of Mount Cameroon, whose beauty drew my eyes throughout the visit.

The journey back to Buea was quiet, because I was sad to leave. Yet I carried home a priceless gift: the memory of a place where nature, culture and kindness meet. One day I shall return, and I am sure it will welcome me as warmly as before.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Describing several places superficially instead of one place in detail.
2. Forgetting the second half of the topic: giving no reasons why the writer would like to visit again.
